title: Yellow Vest
about: A costume vest whose wear and stains became a physical record of a week that changed me.
description:
This track follows two changes that began together during State Arts-In during the fair. Over one intense week, a bright yellow costume vest was physically changed by every handshake, hand on a shoulder, pat on the chest, the repeated touching of its buttons as it was taken on and off, layers of dust, and performance. During that same week, the boy wearing it was also being changed by the people, experiences, and memories around him, except his story didn't end when the vest's did. 

In reality, the vest's transformation happened over one week, while mine continued across the full two weeks of State Arts-In during the fair. The song brings both transformations into the same seven days so their stories can be told together without the difference in timing becoming confusing. By the end of its week, the vest no longer looked like the one I'd first put on. 

By the end of my two weeks, I wasn't quite the same person who had put it on either. One had been changed by countless touches; the other by countless experiences. The song ties those transformations together, letting the visible changes to the vest tell its story while reflecting the less visible changes happening to me.
lyrics: First day of the week, bright as the sun,
Pulled it on without a second thought,
Never guessing what we'd all go through.
Just another costume for another show,
I thought I'd wear that yellow vest...
I never thought it'd wear me in.
That yellow vest wasn't yellow anymore,
Not by the end of the week.
Every smile somebody shared with me.
Dust and sweat, applause and time,
Left their mark where memories lie.
It wasn't dirt that changed its color...
It was seven days of life.
Each one leaving just a little left.
The week kept writing on that cloth
I could've washed the dirt away,
Made it bright like it had been.
That yellow vest wasn't yellow anymore,
I walked into the fair one person,
Walked back home with changed eyes.
Because somewhere in those seven days...
